translations.answer: No. The original author modified to elliptic friction but still exhibited drift; reducing the timestep to 1e-7 did not eliminate the drift, and 1e-6 also showed similar results. Only when the friction coefficients are set to 0 does the behavior become normal, which is only used as a reference for friction-relatedness, not as a solution for tasks with friction. The original thread has no root cause, patch, or passed regression test.
translations.applicability: Strictly limited to the original post MuJoCo 3.3.0, Linux, high-frequency alternating drive and the contact model; cannot be directly extrapolated to all quadruped robots.
translations.credibility.rationale: The answer has not been closed or there is a conflict.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author modified the friction cone to elliptic according to the collaborator's suggestion.
translations.details.attempts.1: Reduced the timestep to 1e-6 and even 1e-7.
translations.details.attempts.2: Set the friction coefficients to 0 as a control.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The collaborator distinguished between the leftward drift in this thread and the slip observed when a friction-cone is subjected to forces in the document.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compared the behavior of pyramidal/elliptic friction cones, timestep from 1e-4 to 1e-7, and friction coefficients set to 0.
translations.details.environments.0: MuJoCo 3.3.0, Linux, original timestep=1e-4, high-frequency alternating motor and friction contact.
translations.details.limits.0: The original issue has not been closed, and there is no maintainer who has fixed it or passed regression test.
translations.details.limits.1: Setting the friction coefficients to 0 is only used as a reference for friction-relatedness, not as a viable solution for tasks with friction.
translations.details.limits.2: Reducing the timestep only lowers the magnitude, and cannot be considered a solution.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Elliptic friction did not eliminate the drift.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The drift was reduced when the timestep was set to 1e-7, but remained; 1e-6 also showed similar results.
translations.details.outcomes.2: When the friction coefficients are set to 0, the original author reported the behavior as normal.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does MuJoCo exhibit unidirectional drift under high-frequency alternating drive and friction contact?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before validating the contact control on real machines, independent convergence checks should be performed on the time step, friction model, and excitation frequency.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original thread only identifies the phenomenon as being related to friction parameters and sensitive to the timestep; the root cause has not been confirmed.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The model continues to drift to the left under alternating drive.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The drift is reduced after reducing the timestep but remains.
translations.source.locator: Issue #2638, phenomenon distinction in issuecomment-2904345405; elliptic tried in issuecomment-2914692123; timestep/friction comparison in issuecomment-2921313334 and 2921314882
translations.source.title: MuJoCo 3.3.0 in High-Frequency Alternating Motor Shows Contact Drift and Unclosed Negative Test
